## 1. Executive Summary

This section provides a high-level overview of the digital transformation strategy, including the vision, business case, key initiatives, and expected outcomes. This summary should be clear, compelling, and understandable to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

### 1.1 Transformation Vision

Articulate the overarching vision for the digital transformation initiative:

- What is the desired future state of the organization after transformation?
- How will digital capabilities enable new business models, customer experiences, or operational efficiencies?
- What competitive advantage or differentiation will be achieved?
- How does this align with the broader organizational strategy?

### 1.2 Strategic Business Drivers

Outline the key business drivers and imperatives for digital transformation:

| Driver Category | Description | Business Impact | Urgency |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| Market Disruption | [E.g., New digital competitors entering the market] | [E.g., Potential loss of market share] | [High/Medium/Low] |
| Customer Expectations | [E.g., Demand for omnichannel experiences] | [E.g., Customer attrition risk] | [High/Medium/Low] |
| Operational Efficiency | [E.g., Rising costs with manual processes] | [E.g., Declining margins] | [High/Medium/Low] |
| Technological Advancement | [E.g., AI and automation potential] | [E.g., Opportunity for new services] | [High/Medium/Low] |
| Regulatory Changes | [E.g., New data privacy requirements] | [E.g., Compliance risk] | [High/Medium/Low] |

### 1.3 Scope and Timeline

Provide a high-level overview of the transformation scope and timeline:

- Transformation timeframe (e.g., 18-36 months)
- Business units or functions in scope
- Key phases and milestones
- Major deliverables and outcomes
- Excluded areas or limitations

### 1.4 Strategic Outcomes and Success Metrics

Summarize the expected outcomes and how success will be measured:

| Outcome Category | Target Outcome | Key Performance Indicators | Target Value | Timeframe |
|------------------|----------------|----------------------------|--------------|-----------|
| Customer Experience | [E.g., Improved customer satisfaction] | [E.g., Net Promoter Score] | [E.g., +15 points] | [E.g., Q4 2026] |
| Operational Efficiency | [E.g., Reduced process time] | [E.g., Process cycle time] | [E.g., -30%] | [E.g., Q2 2026] |
| Revenue Growth | [E.g., New digital revenue streams] | [E.g., Digital revenue %] | [E.g., 25% of total] | [E.g., Q4 2027] |
| Cost Optimization | [E.g., Reduced operational costs] | [E.g., Cost-to-serve] | [E.g., -20%] | [E.g., Q4 2026] |
| Organizational Capability | [E.g., Digital-ready workforce] | [E.g., Digital skill adoption] | [E.g., 80% of staff] | [E.g., Q2 2027] |

### 1.5 Investment Summary

Provide a high-level investment summary:

- Total estimated investment
- Expected ROI and payback period
- Investment categories (technology, people, process change)
- Funding approach

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.
